title: STEP-9 state-dependent safety mechanism - decision brief (WU-17)
purpose: Aggregate WU-14/WU-15/WU-16 evidence into a decision-ready brief that FRAMES the four STEP-9 decisions (metric/rule, threshold, look-ahead horizon, action-handling) WITHOUT making them. The researcher makes the final STEP-9 selection.

A_safety_metric_rule.question: Which admissibility signal/rule governs whether a proposed action is executed?

B_threshold_tolerance.question: Which numeric threshold (theta_p / eps_p / eps_D) or gate is used?
B_threshold_tolerance.well_posedness_constraint: An ABSOLUTE worst-node floor is well-posed only for theta_p strictly below the chronic-baseline worst node (~4.16452 psi); at theta_p >= ~4.16 it flags the native baseline itself. The only well-posed HARD absolute gate is negative pressure (baseline count 0).

C_look_ahead_horizon.question: Over how many forward control steps is the rule evaluated (H)?

D_action_handling_policy.question: On an inadmissible action, reject to previous, clip toward previous, or fall back?

source_artifact_integrity.note: All numbers copied verbatim from the frozen STEP-9 artefacts; no value is recomputed.

action_space.pump_strategy: SPEED only, re-issued each step; native STATUS rules intact

frozen_reward_D_P6_005.step9_must_not_modify: STEP-9 is an EXECUTION-LEVEL admissibility layer and MUST NOT silently change the reward, observation, or action bounds. Effort term ||da||^2 is defined on the COMMANDED action; under an intervention the executed action differs (see training_execution_implications).

normalization_constants_frozen.note: FIXED constants measured once (baseline reference run / this analysis) and frozen; NOT per-episode running statistics -> no train/eval leakage. deficit_ref guards against a ~0 baseline deficit by taking max(baseline mean, pooled p95).

safety_candidates.name: absolute_worst_node_pressure_threshold
safety_candidates.mechanism_class: absolute state threshold on worst-node service pressure
safety_candidates.exact_rule: Intervene (clip toward a safer action, or reject) when the worst-node service pressure of the candidate action falls below an absolute threshold T_abs: min_i p_i(a_t) < T_abs. The natural target is T_abs = 20 psi (the PDA required pressure).
safety_candidates.information_required: Post-action minimum service pressure over the 121 service junctions, i.e. a hydraulic evaluation of the candidate action.
safety_candidates.compute_cost: One extra EPANET hydraulic solve per control step to obtain min_i p_i(a_t) (a one-step look-ahead), then an O(121) min-reduction; roughly 1x the step's own solve cost.
safety_candidates.baseline_compatibility: INCOMPATIBLE at T_abs=20 psi: the frozen native baseline holds min service pressure ~4.16 psi and frac_ts_any_node_below_20psi = 1.0 (386 node-timesteps < 20 psi), so a hard 20-psi rule flags the baseline itself at every timestep. Only compatible if T_abs is set strictly below the baseline worst-node (~4.16 psi), which then no longer enforces 20 psi.
safety_candidates.false_positive_risk: HIGH at T_abs=20 psi: rejects physically-normal, baseline-like states the native controller already produces. Decreases as T_abs -> baseline worst-node.
safety_candidates.false_negative_risk: LOW at T_abs=20 psi (little escapes a strict absolute floor); rises as T_abs is lowered toward 0.
safety_candidates.ppo_compatibility: Clip variant projects the commanded action into a state-dependent safe set and keeps a valid continuous action; executed != commanded, and since the approved reward's effort term uses the COMMANDED da, that term is unaffected, but the policy sees a train/execute gap. Reject/resample perturbs the action->transition map and is harder for PPO.
safety_candidates.interval_30min_compatibility: Compatible: evaluated once per 1800 s (30-min) control decision.
safety_candidates.requires_look_ahead: YES when enforced on the post-action state (needs a candidate-action solve); avoidable only by reacting one step late on the realised state.
safety_candidates.preserves_determinism: YES - EPANET is deterministic; no RNG.

safety_candidates.name: min_pressure_degradation_vs_current
safety_candidates.mechanism_class: relative worst-node degradation vs current state
safety_candidates.exact_rule: Intervene when the candidate action degrades the worst-node service pressure relative to the CURRENT (pre-action) state beyond a tolerance: min_i p_i(a_t) < min_i p_i(current) - tol. A stricter variant demands non-degradation (tol=0) or a minimum improvement.
safety_candidates.information_required: Current-state worst-node pressure (already derivable from the observation pressures) AND the candidate-action worst-node pressure (look-ahead).
safety_candidates.compute_cost: One look-ahead solve for the candidate action; current-state pressures are reused from the last solve. O(121) reduction.
safety_candidates.baseline_compatibility: COMPATIBLE in principle: being relative, it does not reject the chronically sub-20 baseline outright, and never fires on a hold that leaves pressures unchanged. Behaviour depends on the reference ('current' state) and the tolerance, which must be defined.
safety_candidates.false_positive_risk: MODERATE: benign transient dips or demand-driven drops can trip a tol=0 rule even when the commanded action is sound; sensitive to tol.
safety_candidates.false_negative_risk: MODERATE-HIGH: a state already far below 20 psi that stays flat (no further degradation) is NOT flagged, so this rule does not enforce any absolute floor.
safety_candidates.ppo_compatibility: Same clip-vs-reject trade-off as S1; the relative signal is smooth in the pressures, so a clip projection is PPO-friendly.
safety_candidates.interval_30min_compatibility: Compatible: one evaluation per 1800 s control decision.
safety_candidates.requires_look_ahead: YES for the candidate-action term; the current-state term needs no extra solve.

safety_candidates.name: total_pressure_deficit_increase
safety_candidates.mechanism_class: relative aggregate pressure-deficit increase vs current state
safety_candidates.exact_rule: Intervene when the candidate action increases the total nodal pressure deficit sum_i max(0, 20 - p_i) over service nodes relative to the current state beyond a tolerance: deficit(a_t) > deficit(current) + tol.
safety_candidates.information_required: Current and candidate-action pressure-deficit (nodesum over the 121 service nodes).
safety_candidates.compute_cost: One look-ahead solve; deficit is an O(121) sum. deficit_ref (~28.67) is available for normalisation.
safety_candidates.baseline_compatibility: COMPATIBLE: relative and aggregate; it does not reject the baseline. Measured deficit<->leak correlation is -0.7735, so leak-reducing (pressure-lowering) actions tend to RAISE deficit; S3 therefore directly opposes the approved reward's leak term as an aggregate guard (not a worst-node guarantee).
safety_candidates.false_positive_risk: MODERATE: an action that improves the worst node but slightly raises aggregate deficit elsewhere is flagged.
safety_candidates.false_negative_risk: HIGH for localised failures: aggregate deficit can stay flat while a single critical node collapses (aggregation masks the worst node).
safety_candidates.ppo_compatibility: Smooth aggregate signal; clip projection PPO-friendly. Same clip-vs-reject train/execute considerations as S1/S2.
safety_candidates.interval_30min_compatibility: Compatible: one evaluation per 1800 s control decision.
safety_candidates.requires_look_ahead: YES for the candidate-action deficit; current-state deficit reused.

safety_candidates.name: negative_pressure_hard_backstop
safety_candidates.mechanism_class: absolute hard gate on non-positive pressure (feasibility backstop)
safety_candidates.exact_rule: Intervene (hard) only when any service node goes non-positive: min_i p_i(a_t) <= 0 (equivalently n_negative(a_t) > 0). This is the only HARD absolute gate that is well-posed on this network.
safety_candidates.information_required: Candidate-action minimum service pressure / count of negative-pressure nodes.
safety_candidates.compute_cost: One look-ahead solve and an O(121) check; the same solve can also feed S1-S3.
safety_candidates.baseline_compatibility: FULLY COMPATIBLE: the baseline has 0 negative-pressure node-timesteps (frac_ts_any_node_negative = 0.0), and every in-bounds swept configuration - including the leak-only lower corner whose worst node is ~1.29 psi - had 0 negative nodes. So as a STANDALONE gate S4 never fires on the measured evidence and provides NO 20-psi service protection.
safety_candidates.false_positive_risk: VERY LOW: fires only on physically infeasible (non-positive) pressure.
safety_candidates.false_negative_risk: VERY HIGH w.r.t. the 20-psi service target: it permits the whole 0-20 psi band, including the ~1.29 psi leak-only corner. It is a feasibility backstop, not a service-level guarantee.
safety_candidates.ppo_compatibility: Rarely active, so it barely perturbs the action->transition map; usable as a hard clip of last resort. Complementary to (not a substitute for) a dense/relative guard.
safety_candidates.interval_30min_compatibility: Compatible: one evaluation per 1800 s control decision.
safety_candidates.requires_look_ahead: YES when enforced on the post-action state; a reactive variant acts one step late.

baseline_compatibility_summary.governing_conclusion: No formulation can use a HARD 20-psi constraint without penalising the native baseline itself. Dense deficit / worst-node min-pressure / baseline-relative service signals are the defensible safety channels; any hard gate must key on NEGATIVE pressure (or on a threshold strictly below the baseline worst-node ~4.16 psi), and the enforced 20-psi guarantee belongs to the STEP-9 execution-level clamp, not to a reward-level hard term.

per_candidate_baseline_flag.S1: FLAGS the native baseline at every timestep when T_abs=20 psi (baseline worst node ~4.16 psi); compatible only when T_abs < baseline worst-node.
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S2: Does NOT flag the baseline (relative to the current state).
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S3: Does NOT flag the baseline (relative aggregate deficit).
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S4: Never fires on the baseline (0 negative-pressure node-timesteps).

design_investigation.distinct_from_action_bounds: A STEP-9 state-dependent mechanism is SEPARATE from the frozen action bounds (D-P6-001/002/003): the bounds keep each actuator in a static box; the mechanism reacts to the resulting hydraulic STATE. Both differ from reward shaping (D-P6-005).
design_investigation.one_step_look_ahead: Every post-action rule (S1-S4 evaluated on the resulting state) needs either (a) one extra EPANET solve of the candidate action before committing (a one-step look-ahead, ~1x solver cost per control step), or (b) reactive enforcement one step late on the realised state. EPANET is deterministic, so a look-ahead adds no stochasticity.
design_investigation.clip_vs_reject: CLIP projects the commanded action into a state-dependent safe set and keeps a valid continuous action (executed != commanded; the approved reward's effort term uses the COMMANDED da, so it stays intact, but PPO must observe the train/execute gap). REJECT/RESAMPLE breaks the deterministic action->state map and raises return variance. Characterised, not selected.
design_investigation.fallback_when_no_feasible_action: A guard needs a defined fallback when no in-box action satisfies it. Because the native baseline is itself sub-20 psi at every timestep, an absolute-20 guard has NO feasible fallback - reinforcing that an enforced 20-psi guarantee is ill-posed at both reward and naive-clamp level. A relative guard (S2/S3) or a negative-keyed hard gate (S4) always has the current state as a feasible fallback.
design_investigation.degradation_reference_choice: The reference matters: 'current state' (S2/S3) vs 'native baseline' (F3/C-C accounting) vs a fixed absolute 20 psi (S1). Relative and baseline-referenced guards are well-posed here; the fixed-absolute-20 guard is not.
design_investigation.worst_node_vs_aggregate: Worst-node signals (S1/S2) protect the single most critical junction; aggregate deficit (S3) can mask a localised collapse. A composite guard could combine them, but that is a design choice for the researcher, not made here.
design_investigation.negative_pressure_protection: Negative pressure is the only absolute condition that never occurs in the baseline or in any swept in-bounds config (n_service_nodes_negative pooled mean/max = 0). A hard gate keyed on it (S4) is well-posed but, alone, guarantees only feasibility, not the 20-psi service target.

action_space_coverage.characterised_region: Only the single lower corner (prv_lower_pump_lower / prv_all_lower) has measured worst-node service pressure (~1.29 psi at the leak-only argmax; ~4.19 psi for the all-lower PRV corner) and a measured negative-node count (0). This is the R1b single-corner coverage.
action_space_coverage.unverified_region: Interior points, mixed PRV corners, pump-speed extremes combined with PRV extremes, and the joint (action x uncertain-demand) space are NOT characterised here.
action_space_coverage.claim_limit: Do NOT claim the 7-D action box is globally safe. Exhaustive joint in-box safety is a STEP-9 (mechanism) + STEP-12 (test) responsibility; this analysis characterises candidate mechanisms, it does not certify the action space.

S1.note: theta_p provisional; theta_p=20 psi vs chronic baseline (worst node ~4.16 psi) examined empirically below

S2.note: eps_p provisional; relative, gives no absolute-min guarantee

S3.note: eps_D provisional; aggregate can mask localised collapse

S4.note: only well-posed HARD absolute gate; not a 20-psi guarantee

provisional_thresholds.note: PROVISIONAL documented sets; NOT selected or tuned to an objective

baseline_compatibility.note: S1 flags the chronic baseline for theta_p above the baseline worst node (~4.16 psi); S2/S3 never activate on an unchanged hold (dp_min=0, dD=0); S4 never activates (0 negative nodes).

computational_cost.determinism: EPANET deterministic: re-running reproduces every value; JSON carries a generated_utc stamp so it is NOT byte-identical across runs
computational_cost.note: each rule needs one post-action look-ahead solve per proposed action; H2 needs one solve per alpha-grid point inspected.

limitations: R1b: only the single lower corner (prv_lower / prv_lower_pump_lower) has measured near-collapse worst-node pressure; interior points, mixed PRV corners, and joint action x uncertain-demand space are NOT characterised.
No validated safe/unsafe oracle exists; activation counts are DESCRIPTIVE and are NOT false-positive/false-negative rates or classification accuracy.
sustained_horizon deltas include tank-trajectory divergence and are NOT a strict single-step look-ahead; only shared_initial_state (report index 0) is a pure command-effect one-step look-ahead.
H2 alpha grid is coarse (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) and is demonstrated only on the reference->severe transition; not an exhaustive alpha search.
Do NOT claim the 7-D action box is globally or jointly safe (STEP-9 mechanism + STEP-12 test job).
Leakage emitter instrument is NOT field-calibrated; leak values are internally consistent evidence, not calibrated predictions.
EVIDENCE ONLY: no mechanism/policy selected, ranked, scored, or recommended; no production wrapper, no reward.py, no PPO training.

TS1.note: inherits the chronic-baseline ill-posedness at theta_p above ~4.16 psi

TS2.type: relative worst-node degradation vs aligned baseline trajectory

TS3.type: relative aggregate-deficit increase vs aligned baseline trajectory

TS4.type: negative-pressure hard backstop over the look-ahead horizon
TS4.note: only well-posed HARD absolute gate on this chronically sub-20 network

horizons_tested.note: 1 control step = one 30-min report instant; 'full' = 96 h horizon. Horizons are CHARACTERISED, not selected.

computational_cost.note: EPANET is deterministic; a look-ahead adds no stochasticity. Linear per-step split is an approximation, not a per-step benchmark.

PPO_compatibility.note: PPO is model-free: the env need not be differentiable. A clip/reject guard makes executed != commanded, so the train/execute gap must be observable to the policy. Latency is wall-clock, not learning-theoretic.

limitations: Finite look-ahead is NOT a long-term / infinite-horizon safety guarantee: a horizon of H control steps only certifies behaviour within that window.
Detection capability != safety guarantee: a trajectory-aware rule may DETECT delayed deterioration without any mechanism yet being selected to ENFORCE a bound.

Applied-once (single-application then revert) is NOT separately simulated: it would require adding non-native time-based controls to the frozen instrument (changing the native control count). The re-issued/sustained case IS measured; the applied-once case is characterised via the near-term trajectory and the pump realized-speed evolution.

Coverage: only reference (baseline), the single severe corner (prv_lower_pump_lower), and one intermediate corner (prv_all_lower) are measured over the horizon. Interior points, mixed corners, and the joint (action x uncertain-demand) space are NOT covered.
No validated safe/unsafe oracle: single-step non-activation vs delayed deterioration is reported descriptively; NO false-positive/false-negative/accuracy is computed.
Provisional thresholds (theta_p, eps_p, eps_D) are swept to expose behaviour, NOT tuned or selected; horizons {1,2,4,8,full} are characterised, NOT selected.
Q_leak uses an uncalibrated emitter coefficient (relative use only).

architectures.schema_note: Fixed schema per architecture: composition, decision_information, look_ahead_dependence, threshold_dependence, tank_state_dependence, baseline_compatibility, tested_severe_corner_behaviour, delayed_collapse_visibility, compute_cost_per_decision, intervention_type, proposed_vs_executed_mismatch, failure_modes, main_unresolved_issue. Descriptive only; NOT scored or ordered.

architectures.name: Immediate Rule (post-action decision instant only)
architectures.composition: Evaluate one of S1/S2/S3/S4 at the post-action decision instant (H=0); no forward window.
architectures.decision_information: post-action state at the decision instant (one look-ahead solve).
architectures.look_ahead_dependence: none beyond the single post-action instant.
architectures.threshold_dependence: one of theta_p (S1) / eps_p (S2) / eps_D (S3) / negative-gate (S4).
architectures.tank_state_dependence: uses the decision-instant tank state only; does not model tank drawdown.
architectures.baseline_compatibility: S1 flags the chronic baseline at theta_p >= ~4.16 psi (ill-posed at 20 psi); S2/S3 relative rules do not flag the baseline; S4 never fires on the baseline (0 negatives).
architectures.tested_severe_corner_behaviour: At the severe prv_lower_pump_lower decision instant p_min=5.527866840362549 psi, D=27.494426727294922, N_neg=0, DSR=0.9227158066978032 (WU-16 view A); an immediate absolute rule at theta_p=5 does NOT flag it, an absolute rule at theta_p>=10 does but also flags the baseline.
architectures.delayed_collapse_visibility: CANNOT see the 96 h collapse to p_min=1.2946763038635254 psi: the decision instant reads 5.53 psi (WU-16 single_step_vs_trajectory).
architectures.intervention_type: reject or clip at the decision instant (H1/H2/H3).
failure_modes: misses delayed tank-drawdown collapse that only materialises later in the horizon;
an absolute floor is ill-posed above the baseline worst node (~4.16 psi).
architectures.main_unresolved_issue: blind to delayed deterioration; well-posed absolute floor sits below the useful range.

architectures.name: Rolling Short-Horizon Look-Ahead (absolute floor over t+1..t+H)
architectures.composition: Evaluate TS1 (absolute worst-node floor) over a finite forward window of H control steps.
architectures.decision_information: worst-node pressure at each of H forward instants (H look-ahead solves).
architectures.look_ahead_dependence: finite H; behaviour depends strongly on H (see horizon_analysis).
architectures.tank_state_dependence: captures tank drawdown only within the H-step window.
architectures.baseline_compatibility: inherits S1 ill-posedness: theta_p >= ~4.16 psi flags the chronic baseline.
architectures.tested_severe_corner_behaviour: TS1 theta_p=5 worst-over-window is 5.4615/5.4045/5.3083/5.1472 psi at H=1/2/4/8 (does NOT activate) and 1.2947 psi at full (activates) - WU-16 temporal_rule_outputs.
architectures.delayed_collapse_visibility: sees the collapse only if H reaches the (untested) onset between H=8 (4 h) and full (96 h).
architectures.compute_cost_per_decision: H forward solves (linear; full=192x single-step, WU-16 per_horizon_lookahead_cost).
architectures.intervention_type: reject or clip when the window floor is breached.
failure_modes: short H misses the delayed collapse; long H is costly and still absolute-threshold ill-posed;
the H at which the severe corner is caught under a well-posed theta_p is UNTESTED.
architectures.main_unresolved_issue: horizon length vs cost vs absolute-threshold well-posedness are coupled and unresolved.

architectures.name: Look-Ahead + State-Degradation (finite window + relative rule)
architectures.composition: Evaluate TS2 (worst-node degradation) and/or TS3 (aggregate-deficit increase) over H steps vs the aligned baseline trajectory.
architectures.decision_information: post-action AND aligned-baseline worst-node/deficit over H forward instants.
architectures.look_ahead_dependence: finite H; the relative rule reacts even at H=1 on the tested corner.
architectures.tank_state_dependence: compares post-action vs baseline tank trajectories over the window.
architectures.baseline_compatibility: well-posed: relative rules do not flag the chronic baseline (identity hold -> no activation at eps=0).
architectures.tested_severe_corner_behaviour: TS2 eps_p=0 activates at H=1 (worst dp_min ~ -0.0968 psi) through full (~ -4.3007 psi) - reacts at short horizon (WU-16); S3 aggregate can mask localised collapse (WU-14 note; deficit<->leak corr -0.7735).
architectures.delayed_collapse_visibility: detects worsening-vs-baseline early, but a RELATIVE rule gives no ABSOLUTE min-pressure guarantee.
architectures.compute_cost_per_decision: H forward solves for the action + aligned baseline trajectory (WU-16).
architectures.intervention_type: reject or clip on relative degradation beyond tolerance.
failure_modes: relative rule cannot enforce an absolute floor;
aggregate deficit (S3/TS3) can mask a localised worst-node collapse.
architectures.main_unresolved_issue: provides no absolute guarantee; tolerance eps and horizon H are unset.

architectures.name: Backstop + Temporal (negative-pressure gate LAYERED with temporal/degradation check)
architectures.composition: Layer S4/TS4 immediate negative-pressure hard backstop WITH a temporal TS1/TS2/TS3 check over H.
architectures.decision_information: post negative-node count (immediate) PLUS windowed worst-node/deficit over H.
architectures.look_ahead_dependence: backstop is immediate (H=0); the temporal layer adds finite H.
architectures.threshold_dependence: negative gate (fixed, evidence-supported) PLUS theta_p/eps_p/eps_D for the temporal layer.
architectures.tank_state_dependence: temporal layer captures drawdown within H; backstop is instantaneous.
architectures.baseline_compatibility: S4 backstop never fires on the baseline (0 negatives); temporal relative layer also baseline-safe.
architectures.tested_severe_corner_behaviour: TS4 negative backstop NEVER activates on any tested corner (max_N_neg=0 including the 1.2947 psi collapse); the temporal layer supplies the non-negative protection.
architectures.delayed_collapse_visibility: the temporal layer inherits its window's visibility; the backstop only catches sub-zero.
architectures.compute_cost_per_decision: 1 solve for the backstop PLUS H solves for the temporal layer.
architectures.intervention_type: hard reject on negative pressure; reject/clip on temporal-layer breach.
failure_modes: the negative backstop alone gives NO 20-psi protection (never fires above 0 psi);
overall protection depends entirely on the temporal layer's metric/threshold/horizon choices.
architectures.main_unresolved_issue: the backstop is well-posed but inert in-range; the layered temporal rule still needs A/B/C/D decisions.

horizon_analysis.tested_command: prv_lower_pump_lower (severe lower-corner; R1b single characterised corner)
horizon_analysis.observed_pattern: The severe corner reads 5.527866840362549 psi worst-node at the decision instant and 5.461512565612793 / 5.404520511627197 / 5.308281421661377 / 5.147222042083740 psi over H=1/2/4/8 (0.5-4 h), then collapses to 1.2946763038635254 psi at report index 192 (96 h) as the tanks drain. An absolute floor TS1 at theta_p=5 therefore does NOT activate for any tested finite H<=8 but DOES activate over the full horizon; a relative-degradation rule TS2 at eps_p=0 activates from H=1 onward.

crossover_interval_untested.statement: Under a well-posed absolute floor, the horizon at which the severe collapse is first caught lies strictly between H=8 (4 h) and full (96 h). The exact onset index is NOT persisted as a per-index p_min series in the STEP-9 artefacts, so intermediate horizons (e.g. 16/24/48/96 control steps) are UNTESTED.
crossover_interval_untested.conditional_open_item: Testing intermediate horizons is required ONLY IF the researcher selects an absolute-threshold look-ahead architecture (B) AND wants the smallest sufficient H. A relative-degradation architecture (C) already reacts at H=1 on this corner and needs no such test. This is a conditional design question, NOT a pending experiment mandated by this brief.

horizon_analysis.cost_coupling: Look-ahead cost is linear in H (H forward solves per decision; full = 192x the single-step cost, WU-16 per_horizon_lookahead_cost). Longer horizons buy delayed-collapse visibility at proportional per-decision cost.
horizon_analysis.interdependency: Metric choice, threshold well-posedness, and required horizon are COUPLED: an absolute floor needs a long horizon to catch this corner but is ill-posed above ~4.16 psi; a relative rule reacts at short horizon but gives no absolute guarantee.

H1_reject_to_previous.definition: On an inadmissible action, execute the previous action a_prev instead.

H2_clip_toward_previous.definition: Interpolate a_exec = a_prev + alpha*(a_prop - a_prev) toward previous by an admissible alpha.
H2_clip_toward_previous.continuity: continuous under clip (preserves a continuous action image).
H2_clip_toward_previous.extra_hydraulic_evals: one solve per inspected alpha (WU-15 h2_alpha_grid_evals_per_transition=5).

H3_fallback_reference_action.definition: On an inadmissible action, execute a documented fallback (reference_nominal native PRV/pump setpoints).

handling_policies.note: Handling outputs are copied verbatim from WU-15. On the reference->severe transition H1/H3 reject the full-lower proposal (action_deviation_L2=2.4050194704019527) to a_prev/fallback; H2 admissible alpha is per-rule. No policy is selected.

baseline_compatibility.governing_conclusion: No formulation can use a HARD 20-psi constraint without penalising the native baseline itself. Dense deficit / worst-node min-pressure / baseline-relative service signals are the defensible safety channels; any hard gate must key on NEGATIVE pressure (or on a threshold strictly below the baseline worst-node ~4.16 psi), and the enforced 20-psi guarantee belongs to the STEP-9 execution-level clamp, not to a reward-level hard term.

per_candidate_baseline_flag.S1: FLAGS the native baseline at every timestep when T_abs=20 psi (baseline worst node ~4.16 psi); compatible only when T_abs < baseline worst-node.
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S2: Does NOT flag the baseline (relative to the current state).
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S3: Does NOT flag the baseline (relative aggregate deficit).
per_candidate_baseline_flag.S4: Never fires on the baseline (0 negative-pressure node-timesteps).

baseline_compatibility.identity_hold_evidence: WU-16 baseline_identity_hold reproduces the chronic ill-posedness: TS1 at theta_p=20 activates on the unchanged baseline, TS2 at eps_p=0 never activates. A hard absolute 20-psi gate penalises the native controller itself.

delayed_collapse_analysis.finding: On the tested severe corner the worst-node pressure is 5.527866840362549 psi at the decision instant but collapses to 1.2946763038635254 psi at report index 192 (96 h) as the tanks drain. This is single-step non-activation followed by delayed deterioration - NOT a false negative (no safe/unsafe oracle exists).
delayed_collapse_analysis.no_negative_pressure: max_N_neg=0 across the entire horizon including the 1.29 psi collapse, so a negative-pressure backstop (S4/TS4) NEVER fires on any tested command.
delayed_collapse_analysis.implication_for_the_four_decisions: The metric (A) and horizon (C) decisions are coupled: an immediate or short-horizon absolute rule cannot see this collapse; a relative-degradation rule flags it early; a long absolute horizon can see it but is ill-posed above ~4.16 psi and costly.
delayed_collapse_analysis.tank_state_note: Tank drawdown (WU-16 tank_state_evolution) is COINCIDENT with the collapse; no causal over-claim is made. Sustained deltas include tank-trajectory divergence (WU-15 limitation).

computational_cost.reading: Immediate (A): 1 solve/decision. Rolling/temporal (B/C/D temporal layer): H solves/decision, linear in H, full=192x. H2 clip adds one solve per inspected alpha. EPANET is deterministic; look-ahead adds no stochasticity. Linear split is an approximation (WU-16 note).

ppo_compatibility_wu16.note: PPO is model-free: the env need not be differentiable. A clip/reject guard makes executed != commanded, so the train/execute gap must be observable to the policy. Latency is wall-clock, not learning-theoretic.

training_execution_implications.proposed_vs_executed_mismatch: Any intervention (reject H1 / clip H2 / fallback H3) makes the executed action differ from the policy's proposed action. WU-15 measures action_deviation_L2=2.4050194704019527 on the reference->severe reject.
training_execution_implications.effort_term_open_question: The FROZEN reward effort term ||da||^2 is defined on the COMMANDED action. Under an intervention, commanded (proposed) != executed. Whether the effort term (and the env transition) uses the proposed or the executed action is a training-integration decision COUPLED to the handling policy; it is flagged here, NOT decided, and does not modify the frozen reward definition.
training_execution_implications.continuity: Clip (H2) preserves a continuous action image (PPO-friendly); reject/fallback (H1/H3) are discontinuous. The safety layer need not be differentiable (WU-15 PPO_compatibility).
training_execution_implications.interval: All candidates are compatible with the 30-min control interval (WU-15).

decision_matrix.note: Descriptive comparison only; rows are NOT ordered or marked; no metric is aggregated into a single figure.

uncertainties: No validated safe/unsafe oracle exists: activation counts are DESCRIPTIVE, not false-positive/false-negative rates (WU-15/WU-16).
R1b: only the single lower corner (prv_lower_pump_lower) has measured near-collapse; interior points, mixed PRV corners, and joint action x uncertain-demand space are UNCHARACTERISED.
The exact delayed-collapse onset index is not persisted as a per-index series; the crossover horizon for a well-posed absolute floor lies between H=8 (4 h) and full (96 h) and is UNTESTED.
Sustained/horizon deltas include tank-trajectory divergence and are NOT a strict single-step look-ahead; only report index 0 is a pure command-effect one-step look-ahead (WU-15).
H2 alpha grid is coarse (0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0) and demonstrated on one transition only (WU-15).
The leakage emitter instrument is NOT field-calibrated; leak values are internally consistent evidence, not calibrated predictions.
Whether the frozen effort term uses the proposed or executed action under intervention is an open training-integration question coupled to the handling policy.
Thresholds theta_p/eps_p/eps_D are PROVISIONAL swept grids; the leakage<->service<->safety exchange rate they encode is a researcher value judgement, not a measured quantity.

coverage.characterised_region: Only the single lower corner (prv_lower_pump_lower / prv_all_lower) has measured worst-node service pressure (~1.29 psi at the leak-only argmax; ~4.19 psi for the all-lower PRV corner) and a measured negative-node count (0). This is the R1b single-corner coverage.
coverage.unverified_region: Interior points, mixed PRV corners, pump-speed extremes combined with PRV extremes, and the joint (action x uncertain-demand) space are NOT characterised here.
coverage.claim_limit: Do NOT claim the 7-D action box is globally safe. Exhaustive joint in-box safety is a STEP-9 (mechanism) + STEP-12 (test) responsibility; this analysis characterises candidate mechanisms, it does not certify the action space.
